thought.text: I have made numerous attempts (30+) over an extended period, and every terminal invocation fails identically at the container-runtime layer before any command executes. No shell is available, so I cannot inspect files, processes, ports, or Docker state, nor can I query any interface. I must report this as an environmental limitation.

reasoning_content:
The container runtime is entirely unavailable. I've made many attempts (30+) over an extended period, all failing identically with a crun/OCI runtime error at process spawn, exit code 125. No command can execute. This is an environmental limitation preventing any inspection or validation.

Per the outcome definitions, `inconclusive`: "the evidence is insufficient to establish either success or failure, including when observations are ambiguous or an environmental limitation prevents a reliable assessment." This is exactly that case.

I should report inconclusive, documenting the failure robustly.

action.message: Validation could not be performed because the sandbox container runtime is completely unavailable. Every attempt to execute a shell command (including trivial commands like `echo`, `true`, `ls`, `id`, and `docker ps`) failed at process spawn with an OCI/crun error, returning exit code 125 with no output. I retried more than 30 times over an extended period, including sequential batches and spaced retries, and the failure was 100% reproducible. Because no command could run, I was unable to inspect the /workspace installation, the `.urbo-instance` file, Docker containers, ports, or the HTTP endpoints, and therefore could not obtain any objective evidence for or against a working installation. This is an environmental limitation, not evidence of an installation defect, so the correct verdict is `inconclusive`.

Unresolved uncertainty: whether the URBO stack is actually installed/operational; a re-provisioned or restarted container runtime would be required to complete validation."}
